words.meaning: to deliberately give something less urgency or importance than other work
words.example: We should deprioritize cosmetic changes until the reliability issues are resolved.

words.meaning: to narrow a larger group of options to a smaller set of finalists
words.example: The committee will downselect the eight proposals to three by Friday.

words.meaning: involving repeated observations of the same people or subjects over time
words.example: The longitudinal study showed that customer trust improved steadily after the policy change.

words.meaning: able to be repeated independently with the same or very similar results
words.example: Please document each step so the analysis is reproducible by another team.

words.meaning: to return a person, asset, or resource to its country or place of origin
words.example: The company plans to repatriate part of its overseas earnings next quarter.

phrases.meaning: to use up the remaining time, often to preserve an advantage or avoid action
phrases.example: The vendor seemed to be running the clock out instead of answering our contract questions.

phrases.meaning: to interpret limited clues in order to predict what is likely to happen
phrases.example: Reading the tea leaves, I think leadership will approve the smaller pilot.

phrases.meaning: to understand or gain control of something complicated
phrases.example: Give me a day to get my arms around the new reporting requirements.

phrases.meaning: to choose the option most likely to succeed based on the odds
phrases.example: We played the percentages and launched first in the market with the strongest demand.

phrases.meaning: experiencing a period of unusually fast, energetic, or successful activity
phrases.example: The sales team has been on a tear since the new pricing plan rolled out.
